articles.title: Brain “noise” during speech processing is linked to verbal communication skills in autistic youth
articles.summary: A new study found that background electrical brain activity while listening to speech relates to everyday verbal communication skills in autistic children and teens, suggesting that higher neural noise may affect practical language use.

articles.title: Diversity in graduate school linked to higher starting salaries
articles.summary: A large analysis of business and law school graduates reveals that attending classes with a racially diverse student body is linked to higher median starting salaries, suggesting that diversity initiatives offer tangible economic benefits for all students.

articles.title: Scientists map the brain’s attention networks in children with ADHD
articles.summary: New neuroimaging research reveals that the functional brain networks supporting attention operate on a continuous spectrum, looking functionally identical in children whether or not they have a diagnosis of ADHD.

articles.summary: Researchers exploring new treatments for adult ADHD found that a digital training app improved participants' perceived quality of life. Users felt their mental focus improved, though cognitive tests did not provide evidence of these changes.

articles.title: Newborn brains respond more strongly to crying than to speech, study finds
articles.summary: A new brain imaging study reveals that newborn babies respond more strongly to infant cries than to spoken language. The findings suggest that a baby's physical ability to vocalize shapes how their brain processes communicative sounds from birth.

articles.title: Memory retrieval deficits tied to worse symptoms in people with obsessive-compulsive disorder
articles.summary: Patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder often recall broad summaries of events rather than specific, detailed memories. New research linking this cognitive trait to mental inflexibility and worsening symptoms could pave the way for novel therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Long-term study reveals how childhood ADHD impacts adult mental health, cognition, and daily life
articles.summary: New longitudinal research shows childhood ADHD increases the likelihood of adult mental health challenges and lower educational attainment. Despite these elevated risks, researchers emphasize that many adults with childhood ADHD function comparably to their peers.

articles.title: A hidden Alzheimer’s tipping point may decide who gets dementia
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a possible tipping point that helps determine whether Alzheimer’s-related brain changes lead to dementia. The key may lie in how the brain’s immune cells respond to plaques and tau, offering a promising new target for treatments designed to extend cognitive resilience.

articles.title: Inside the Backrooms: The internet’s creepiest place is becoming a tourist attraction
articles.summary: The Backrooms began as a single eerie image of empty yellow rooms, but internet users transformed it into a vast fictional world that feels disturbingly real. Through videos, games, maps, survival guides and social media stories, audiences do more than watch the horror unfold. They help build and explore it. Researchers suggest this popularity reflects a new kind of digital tourism, where people emotionally enter imaginary places filled with mystery, nostalgia and unease.

articles.title: Plant-based compounds in berries and tea may help delay brain aging
articles.summary: A new scientific review suggests that polyphenols—natural compounds found in berries, tea, and olive oil—may help protect the brain from age-related decline. However, researchers emphasize eating whole foods over relying on high-dose supplements.

articles.title: Anxiety and feelings of entrapment may connect psychotic distress to suicidal ideation
articles.summary: A new study reveals that the emotional distress caused by hallucinations and delusions is strongly linked to suicidal thoughts. This connection operates through severe anxiety and feelings of entrapment, highlighting the importance of easing a person's subjective emotional pain.

articles.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain’s food craving circuit
articles.summary: Newer oral drugs related to semaglutide medications such as Ozempic reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The finding could open new avenues for understanding food cravings and potentially treating substance use disorder.

articles.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
articles.summary: Even mild inflammation during pregnancy led mouse offspring to develop persistent brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors, and increased seizure risk. Remarkably, one dose of rapamycin improved nearly all of these problems within about two hours. The benefits were temporary, but they suggest that adult brain circuits may remain far more adaptable than previously believed.

articles.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
articles.summary: Scientists expected SuperAgers might simply inherit fewer Alzheimer’s-related risks, but their genes looked much like those of typical older adults. Their extraordinary memories may instead come from still-unknown protective forces involving the brain, body, lifestyle, and environment.
